newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl urges German SPD to compromise on tax reform.
newsitem.headline: Kohl urges German SPD to compromise on tax reform.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl urged the opposition Social Democrats (SPD) on Friday to reach a compromise on government tax reforms, saying a deal could be reached quickly in parliamentary mediation.
Kohl also stood by a coalition deal to cut the solidarity income tax surcharge next year, which has been thrown into doubt by some politicians in his three-party ruling alliance.
Finance Minister Theo Waigel's package of 30 billion
marks in income and corporate tax cuts was thrown out of the upper house of parliament by the SPD majority, condemning it to a tortuous path through legislative mediation.

"It now depends on the SPD majority in the mediation committee whether the tax reform can take effect as planned," he said. "We, the coalition, are ready to compromise. But we are not willing to give up on key elements of the tax reform."
Kohl said SPD leader Oskar Lafontaine's refusal to do a deal on tax amounted to "treason against the unemployed".

He sought to quell criticism by some coalition politicians of an earlier deal to cut the solidarity surcharge -- raised to finance the rebuilding of eastern Germany -- by two points to 5.5 percent. "The reduction of the solidarity surcharge from January 1998 has been agreed by the coalition."
